I disagree with everything you said. It's a feminist movie about a woman who hasn't been indoctrinated by society's expectations yet and who questions everything and in the end finds herself and her place in society.

Not a single man can tell her what to do her trap her. She disobeys her "father", her lover and her husband. 

She is her own person and in the end takes over and fulfills her dreams and ambitions by becoming a doctor.

I didn’t see it that way or felt the movie was any ambiguous in its meaning. The Favorite and now Poor Things are both very feminist with Poor Things exploring the gender construct and expectations in what is a typical Yorgos Lanthimos style. Slightly off the topic but I thought Yorgos’ style really comes together in this picture - from those extreme wide angle lenses to music and disguised macabre

Unfortunately I think that’s a simplification of the film’s themes- like others here this movie at the end of the day is optimistic and personally I think the theme can really be summed up in Father’s last words “it’s all… very interesting” 

It’s honestly the opposite of what you’re saying here. Through all the horrible things, Bella still keeps an excitement for learning and for life. 

BUT! If you want something about the themes you’re talking about (our obsession with horrible things) check out Funny Games or Man Bites Dog

Lol. No offense buddy, but this reads as one of the most "we live in a society!"  posts ever written. You used GoT and a single movie as your example.

My dude. There are 700 films coming out every year. Couple hundred TV shows. How in god's green Earth do these two examples paint a picture of society as a whole. 

You're looking through a keyhole and describing the world as keyhole shaped, not realizing there are thousands of other doors.

I agree with most of what you said and I think it goes beyond that and is also a socioeconomic critique as well. I love discussing films with people and seeing other view points even if I disagree, but I have no idea where OP got his weirdly puritanical viewpoint. It’s like they went in with that frame of view already in place.

It also gives me a little laugh that in such a gorgeous movie, all OP sees is disgusting, vile and monstrous.

I totally agree with your interpretation and I think anyone that disagrees is not able to look at our current society from a completely objective perspective due to how numb we’ve become to the things you mentioned. We think we’re so much more enlightened than we used to be as humans due to advances in technology and we think there’s no way we can revert back to some of the terrible, animalistic atrocities that we’ve committed in the past but we’re still seeing these things occur daily around the world despite our “enlightened” state, it maybe just looks a little bit different than it did in the past.
You can’t claim to know an objective truth when you lack comprehension skills.
"Feminist" written by a middle school student
There is also the fact she disobeys "god" to a certain extent, as there is at least some parallelism between her and Eve, although not as intense

It's tonally different but is not disimilar to movies like Species or Fifth Element, where you have a rapidly advancing intelligence learning all the wrong lessons from our patriarchal society, and ends up using it's own logic to thwart it. The intent being that the audience might realize the flaws inherent to that structure. 
I'm not saying this is all that's going on in the movie, but it's the theme you've latched onto the strongest. 

Seems like it was successful?
